title: Domestic races differ greatly externally but little internally

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Domestic races differ greatly externally but little internally

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because man can select mainly on externally visible deviations, domestic races differ greatly in external characters and relatively slightly in internal parts or organs.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We can, I think, further understand the frequently abnormal character of our domestic races, and likewise their differences being so great in external characters and relatively so slight in internal parts or organs.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter I, “Variation under Domestication”; section “Methodical and Unconscious Selection”. Scope: domestic races of animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch01-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The distinction can be quantified and relevant public resources exist, but internal measurements are sparse and trait scaling is consequential. Current data cover a subset of domestic animals.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure standardized among-breed variance in external morphology and internal anatomy across domestic species, then compare their effect-size distributions. Consistently larger external divergence supports the claim; similar internal divergence refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
External and internal traits have no natural common scale.

Internal anatomy is sampled far less densely.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.68
discriminating power: 0.65
data adequacy: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.62
operationalizability: 0.76

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The external-versus-internal partition is straightforward wherever both are measured, and 3D archives contain pieces of it for dogs and a few other animals. They are not a designed comparative sample of domestic races, and soft anatomy is largely missing. A result for skulls and limb bones would be a restricted proxy for the full contrast.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Partition multivariate disparity among breeds into external characters and internal organs, using size-corrected measurements from the same individuals. Greater external disparity would support the contrast; equal or greater internal disparity would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Allometry and body-size divergence move internal organs without any direct selection on them.

Few breeds have both external and internal measurements on a common sample.

Soft organs are rarely preserved in the scan collections that are public.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.36
discriminating power: 0.48
data existence: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.7
data adequacy: 0.28
